content.text:
I'd go with Harel's "מניות" track. It went up the most by far, 24.04% over 3 years and 14.64% over 5. The S&P one my friends talk about only did 13.7%. The fees are all about the same, around 0.55%, which sounds like nothing. I'm fairly sure about which track, but I have no idea how to actually put the money in. There's no button on the page to join. And it's all under "קופת גמל להשקעה", which sounds like a pension thing for older people, so I'm not sure it's even the right product for my 30,000.

**How it went:**
- **Top of the page:** I saw the big "הראל" heading and a row of products. "קופת גמל להשקעה 16" was already picked, so I stayed on it. I noticed "קרן השתלמות" next to it but didn't open it. Then I saw the track buttons and spotted "עוקב מדד S&P 500".
- **The table:** I went down it reading the name on the right and the big green numbers. Most tracks just say "פחות מ־3 שנים" instead of a return, so there was nothing to compare. Only three or four have real numbers. "מניות" jumped out at 24.04%. The fees column is 0.54% to 0.61%, all basically the same.
- **The middle column:** It shows "מניות" and "מט"ח" percentages with little rings. I didn't get it. The S&P one says 99% and 99%, and I don't know how both can be 99%.
- **Bottom of the table:** There's a line "תקרה בחוק: 1.05%… 4% מההפקדה". I don't know what that's about, and I skipped the grey text around it.
- **Lower down:** Folds for "קרנות מחקות", "קרנות סל", "מה כתוב במסמכים של הראל" and a lot more. I didn't open any of them. Then a search box and the footer, and that was the end.

**What I didn't get:** "מט"ח", "חשיפה למניות ולמט"ח", "ההפקדה" vs "ההיסכון", "תשואה שנתית ממוצעת, לפני דמי ניהול", the "קופה" numbers like 8522, and whether "קופת גמל להשקעה" is something I'm even allowed to use at 26.

**What bugged me:** The page tells me what it is and how it did, but not what to do next. I'd have closed it about there and asked someone at work. Also the first row is "אשראי ואג"ח" with 106 million and no return at all, which is a strange thing to show first.
